artworks.title: Death of Talos (volute-krater)
artworks.description: The name-vase in Ruvo: winged figures pull the bronze pin from Talos' ankle as ichor drains — Apollonius' Crete automaton dying on Attic red-figure clay.

artworks.title: Jason and Medea beside Talos
artworks.description: Van der Borcht's engraving stages the Argonauts before the bronze giant — Renaissance print culture keeping Talos' ankle-pin death in circulation.

artworks.title: Talos (Argonaut cycle)
artworks.description: Carstens' neoclassical plate from the Argonautenzug: Talos as monumental bronze threat — late-eighteenth-century line for the guardian of Crete.

artworks.title: Didrachm of Phaistos (Talos)
artworks.description: Silver didrachm of Phaistos in the Cabinet des Médailles: winged Talos as the city's bronze guardian — Crete minting its automaton into civic identity.

artworks.title: Talos (sculpture, Cambridge)
artworks.description: Ayrton's bronze Talos in Cambridge — modern sculpture returning the Cretan automaton as a striding metal body in the open air.

films.title: Jason and the Argonauts
films.description: Ray Harryhausen's stop-motion Talos — the bronze giant who stalks the Argo — remains the defining modern image of Crete's automaton.

popCulture.title: Argonautica
popCulture.creator: Apollonius of Rhodes
popCulture.description: Book IV — Medea's enchantment, the ankle pin, and ichor draining from bronze: the canonical death of Talos.

popCulture.title: Talos
popCulture.description: Hephaestus' bronze guardian of Crete — circling the island three times a day until the Argonauts unpinned his life.
